newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says economy stable, inflation in check.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says economy stable, inflation in check.

text.p: Indonesia announced a healthy February trade surplus and a moderate rise in April prices on Wednesday and the government as well as analysts said the economy was in good shape.

"The development of our economy and monetary system were reported in a good state at the cabinet meeting," Information Minister Harmoko told reporters after the regular monthly cabinet meeting chaired by President Suharto.
"We concluded our economy was stable despite the ongoing campaign for general elections," he added.

Analysts have previously said the campaign for the May 29 general elections, which started last month, could have some short-term effects on the economy because of the potential for violence and food shortages.

The cabinet meeting was told that inflation rose 0.56 percent month-on-month in April against a fall of 0.12 percent in March, Harmoko said. Year-on-year inflation in April was up 4.95 percent against an increase of 5.17 percent in March.
Harmoko said inflationary pressure in the housing and service sectors was responsible for the moderate increase in the April index.
He said also Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $964.3 million in February against $575.4 million in January.
Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said the country's economic fundamentals were strong and there was no significant impact on the economy because of the upcoming general election.

"It's quite encouraging. Month-on-month (seasonally adjusted on a three-month moving average basis) we have seen a recovery (in non-oil exports) in January and February," said Vincent Low, an economist at JP Morgan in Singapore.

Total exports in February were valued at $4.06 billion, with oil and gas exports at $1.04 billion. Comparable figures for January were $4.24 billion and $1.23 billion. Imports fell to $3.09 billion in February from $3.67 billion in January.
"I think growth rates are also picking up on a year-on-year basis. That is a good sign," Low told Reuters.
"It's a good set of figures. The export numbers are still enjoying the benefit of higher oil prices," Desmond Supple, head of research for Asian currencies at BZW Barclays in Singapore, said.
Harmoko said Suharto had ordered cabinet ministers to keep prices in check and to remain watchful for any inflationary pressures.
"The president said we must remain cautious. Bulog (the state commodities regulator) must initiate market operations in basic goods to prevent speculation," Harmoko said.

Indonesia posted an inflation rate of 6.47 percent for the 1996 calendar year, compared with 8.64 percent in 1995. The government has forecast an inflation rate of six percent for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1.
Coordinating Minister of Economic Affairs Saleh Afiff said the government was preparing a package of economic deregulation measures, including a further cut in import tariffs.
The government has spoken previously about a new package but has not given any details.
